surface: Malicious-hardware / supply-chain implant detection (key=implant). Threat: CryptoBilis-style display-bus logger/exfil MCU behind the screen, PCB implants, swapped components, probe residue, reseller tampering before first power. Scope read: secure/src/hw/{tamp,tamp_reason,tzic,bhk,se_power,boot_pulse,usb_hw,rng,dbgmcu,aw99703,aw21036,se_i2c_probe,spi_hw,lcd_nv3007}.rs, secure/src/board/pq1.rs, secure/src/sau.rs, secure/src/first_boot/, secure/src/measured_boot.rs, secure/src/ui/{secret_text,seed_wizard,px/assets}.rs, secure/src/nsc/{mod,prodtest}.rs, fsbl/src/{main,verify,optbytes,sau,render,aw99703,nv3007}.rs, shared/src/lockdown.rs, tools/{verify_ship_state.py,verify-fsbl-identity.sh,factory-provisioning-verify.sh}, docs/hardware/*, docs/provisioning/*, docs/security/{HARDENING,threat-model,measured-boot,red-teaming,user-device-verification,production-security,supply-chain-defense-research-brief}.md, adversarial-review playbooks, README shipping checklist, CLAUDE.md invariant #10, and `gh issue list` searches (implant/tamper/supply chain/mesh/attestation/genuine/interposer/display/backlight/VBUS/enclosure/first power/RDP-0/verify flash/SWD/SBU/transparency log/birth certificate/tamper-evident/DNP/anti-counterfeit/UID). Bottom line: the repo's ONLY implemented defence against a pre-first-power implant is 'firmware bytes are verifiable over SWD at RDP-0' (off-device, bench-profile tooling) plus encrypted SE tunnels; there is NO code path that can detect a hardware implant on the display SPI bus, the buttons, or the PCB, and the docs say so honestly (user-device-verification.md 'What this explicitly does NOT prove' item 1). Everything board-level (mesh, case switch, EMI can, temp sensor, tamper-evident packaging, SE genuine-check, birth certificate/transparency log, MCU anti-counterfeit probes) is requirements/issue-only.

has.item: RDP-0 shipping model + first-boot Phase A ship-profile verification (TZEN/RDP/SECWM/SECBOOTADD0/WRP1A/OEM) before the RDP-2 self-lock
evidence: secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:165-190 (run_pre_lock_and_maybe_lock → lockdown::verify_ship_profile, halt UNLOCKED on mismatch via halt_first_boot)
has.notes: Only compiled under `rdp2-self-lock` (implies mode-production + dual-se); every `mode-production + optiga-trust-m` build is rejected by the OPTIGA_S2_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED fence, so this code cannot be linked into a shipping image today. WRP1A and OEM-lock predicates are fail-CLOSED while `WRP1A_MASK_PINNED`/`OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED` are false (shared/src/lockdown.rs:290, :445), i.e. the production profile check cannot pass on real silicon until the register layouts are bench-pinned (#46, #270). Silicon-lockdown playbook SL9 notes the OPTR check is a spot-check, not an exact masked compare. On-device verification is explicitly worth zero against interdiction (tools/verify_ship_state.py:9-16; Draft 1.2 §2.2) — it catches factory escapes, not implants.

gaps.gap: No mechanism, in code or design, can detect a logger/injector on the LCD SPI bus (PA4/PA5/PA7), the DC/RST/TE lines, or the display module connector. The panel is write-only, PA6/MISO is NC, the FSBL/secure-world render verdict only proves the SPI peripheral finished, and the 24 seed words cross that bus as plaintext pixels in the wizard. This is the exact CryptoBilis shape.
gaps.tracked_in: Not tracked as an issue. Named only as an accepted residual in docs/security/user-device-verification.md ('What this explicitly does NOT prove' item 1) and fsbl/src/render.rs:50-80. Adjacent: #237 (OLED emanation, seed-wizard scope), #260 (constant-pixel encoding), #705 (backlight).

owner_decisions: Ship at RDP-0 with user-verifiable flash/option-bytes/OTP over SWD before first power; first field boot self-locks RDP-2; NO factory/fixture RDP-2 burn and NO factory-held final pairing secret (owner 2026-07-14, work-todo #36; CLAUDE.md 'Shipping model'). Any implant-detection proposal must not reintroduce a factory lock or a factory-held secret.

Invariant #10 verify-once-physically trust chain (owner 2026-07-21): the FSBL must own the display for its boot-time fingerprint window; 'a later fake screen is the accepted residual — the boot-time window is the anchor'; no runtime write path may touch the FSBL range; WRP-set → RDP-2 ordering mandatory. Proposals that rely on post-boot display attestation are outside the accepted anchor.

Option B (owner 2026-07-21, recorded in tools/verify_ship_state.py and Makefile verify-ship-state): on-device self-verification at RDP-0 is worth zero against interdiction; the load-bearing check is OFF-device. Do not propose on-device 'genuine firmware' self-checks as implant/interdiction defences.
Phase A RDP-2 burn must be CONFIRM-GATED on the trusted UI (owner 2026-07-17); a profile mismatch halts UNLOCKED so a bad flash is never turned into an RDP-2 brick (first_boot/mod.rs:165-190).

ML-KEM-1024 inner wrap DESCOPED 2026-07-07 — do not re-raise (work-todo #9): the I2C bus-tap residual (an implant on I2C1/I2C4 during a live unlock) is ACCEPTED at Grover-2^64/Cat-1 per tunnel, conditional on per-device final rotation being load-bearing. Implant research may strengthen rotation/replay freshness but must not re-propose a PQ KEM wrap.
TROPIC01 removed 2026-07-14 — dual-SE (OPTIGA + SE050) only; no third SE as an attestation anchor.

OPTIGA S-1/S-2/S-3 lockdown ship-blockers are deferred BY DESIGN (chips cost money, LcsO is irreversible; memory note). The OPTIGA_S2_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED fence makes every mode-production + optiga-trust-m build (and therefore rdp2-self-lock) unbuildable today; this is not avoidance.

tamp-wipe/tzic-wipe are default-OFF on bench builds and FORCED ON for shipping dual-SE images via the nsc/mod.rs fence (audit tz-tamper 20260611 MEDIUM-1); a bench board under probe-rs must not brick on a false ITAMP9. Any proposal to make tamper detection stricter must preserve the bench/prod split.

Pixel UI (ui-px) owner decisions 2026-09-22/23/24: atlas lives in the NS slot and is SHA-256-pinned; scroll-to-end gate is ON; sign gesture is the two-button chord. ui-px stays out of make release until the flash lever lands. Display-integrity proposals touching the sign gesture or atlas placement must not re-litigate these.
FSBL fingerprint hold = 4 s (owner 2026-09-24, down from 10 s), non-dismissible; trading reading time for boot latency is an owner call.
SHAKE-vs-SHA2 is DECIDED (stay on plain SHA-2); SE050 SCP03 stays on the BHK axis (answered 2026-09-21, memory). Not implant-specific but constrain any 'swap the primitive/root' suggestions.

Factory responsibilities (first-boot-provisioning.md 'Done at the FACTORY'): set every option byte EXCEPT RDP, burn the per-device OTP master, provision SE-internal structure on transport keysets, read-back QA over SWD; the line must not generate or retain final pairing secrets (README §B).
